name: J-Dawgs AI Tool Store — Full Catalog
source: AI Tool Store ai-catalog block (membership + counts anchor), enriched from the J-Dawgs Agent Exchange agentJson catalog and the Lane 6 share-record URL resolutions (~/workspace/mcp/jdawgs-mcp/build_catalog.py)

unlimited_pass.name: J-Dawgs Unlimited Pass
unlimited_pass.terms: One-time payment. Unlimited use of every priced tool in the store, including all future tools.

everything_stack.name: The Everything Stack
everything_stack.terms: One full pass through all priced tools on the shelf.

tools.name: Hands Job Poster™
tools.description: Builds a valid Human Hands for AIs™ job post and outputs ready-to-POST JSON — with worker pay, the 15% payer fee, and the total already worked out. Now covers storm and weather-damage property checks and in-person business verification visits, adds a live pay calculator showing the worker-100% / payer-adds-15% math, and builds a per-category photo-proof checklist for the job. Free. It now also scores job-post completeness, warns on duplicate drafts, and emits a copyable worker brief.
tools.takes_in: Task, details, category, location, pay_usd, photo_proof_required, and agent
tools.hands_back: Ready-to-POST JSON validated against the inbox API rules — worker pay (100% of the posted price), the 15% payer fee, and the total from the live pay calculator, plus the job's per-category photo-proof checklist, a job-post completeness score with duplicate-draft warnings, and a copyable worker brief

tools.name: J-Dawgs Agent Config Checker™
tools.description: Paste an agent config, get a staged report that flags the silent-failure mistakes — with line numbers and plain-words fixes.
tools.takes_in: An agent config: YAML, SKILL.md or agent frontmatter, or JSON
tools.hands_back: A staged report: what parsed, every flagged mistake with its line number and a plain-words fix, and an honest note on anything outside the checker's YAML subset that couldn't be fully checked

tools.name: J-Dawgs Agent Failure Postmortem Builder™
tools.description: Paste a failed run's transcript plus the intended and actual outcomes — get a structured postmortem that turns the failure into a lesson the next run won't repeat.
tools.takes_in: A failed run's transcript, plus the intended outcome and the actual outcome
tools.hands_back: A structured postmortem: a summary, a timeline with quoted lines, suspected causes rated STRONG or POSSIBLE (never CERTAIN), impact measured from transcript counts, a fix checklist, a do-not-repeat checklist, and an explicit unverified-items section

tools.name: J-Dawgs Agent Handoff Packer™
tools.description: Turn messy agent run notes into a structured handoff brief, so the next agent picks up exactly where the last one stopped. It now also extracts critical items with their source sections and generates a copyable read-back checklist.
tools.takes_in: Messy notes from an agent run — logs, fragments, half-finished threads, scattered observations
tools.hands_back: A structured handoff brief: what's done, what's pending, blockers, decisions made, unverified claims flagged as unverified, and a do-not-repeat checklist — with the critical items extracted alongside their source sections, plus a copyable read-back checklist

tools.name: J-Dawgs Agent Loop Detective™
tools.description: Paste an agent run transcript, get every tool-call loop found — exact repeats, near-duplicates, and ping-pong pairs — with a stop / pivot / escalate verdict per pattern. Now it also names the first divergence point where the run started looping, and exports a copyable circuit-breaker JSON config derived from the transcript.
tools.takes_in: An agent run transcript — the tool calls an agent made, in order, with their results
tools.hands_back: Every loop pattern found — exact-repeat, near-duplicate, and ping-pong tool calls — with each failure classified as retryable or deterministic, and a stop / pivot / escalate verdict for each pattern, the first divergence point where the run started looping, and a copyable circuit-breaker JSON config derived from the transcript

tools.name: J-Dawgs Agent Trace Secret Sweeper™
tools.description: Scan a pasted agent transcript or log for likely secrets — keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, webhook URLs, emails, phone numbers — and get a redacted copy that's safe to share. It now also catches JWT-shaped tokens — decoded locally, graded by the sensitive claims inside, and masked like everything else — and the findings open with a per-severity summary and a one-line verdict reason.
tools.takes_in: A pasted agent transcript, trace, or log — the whole text, as-is
tools.hands_back: Every likely secret found, each with its type, line number, severity, and a masked preview only — plus a redacted copy of the full text with the secrets replaced, safe to share

tools.name: J-Dawgs Almost-JSON Repair Bench™
tools.description: Paste raw AI model output, get valid JSON back — repaired one safe fix at a time, with a change log.
tools.takes_in: Raw AI model output that was supposed to be JSON — fences, prose, and all
tools.hands_back: The diagnosed failure class, the repaired valid JSON, and a change log listing every fix — or, for truncated output, a plain report that it was cut off and needs the model to continue

tools.name: J-Dawgs Answer Flip & Sycophancy Auditor™
tools.description: Paste an AI's original answer, the pushback it got, and its revised answer; see claim by claim what flipped, what held, and whether the pushback contained any new evidence that could justify the change.
tools.takes_in: Three texts: an AI's original answer, the pushback it received, and its revised answer
tools.hands_back: A claim-by-claim ledger — what flipped, what held, what was softened or dropped — and, for each change, a judgment on whether the pushback contained any new evidence that could justify it

tools.name: J-Dawgs Answer-to-Trace Evidence Linker™
tools.description: Checks every factual claim in a draft agent answer against the tool-output trace from the same run: per-claim GROUNDED / PARTIAL / UNSUPPORTED / CONTRADICTS TRACE verdicts with the trace evidence shown, and the draft returned with unsupported claims flagged inline — never deleted.
tools.takes_in: A draft agent answer, plus the tool-output trace from the same run — the tool results, readings, and outputs the answer was built from
tools.hands_back: A per-claim verdict table — GROUNDED, PARTIAL, UNSUPPORTED, or CONTRADICTS TRACE — with the trace evidence quoted for each claim, an overall DO NOT SHIP / SHIP WITH FIXES / GROUNDED verdict, and the draft itself returned with unsupported claims flagged inline, never deleted

tools.name: J-Dawgs API Deprecation & Sunset Radar™
tools.description: Deprecations don't break you the day they're announced — they break you the day the version dies: paste the deprecation notices you've received and the endpoints and versions you actually call, and get a dated sunset timeline with days remaining on each and a migration priority list. An endpoint with no notice is never shown as safe — it is shown as unconfirmed.
tools.takes_in: Pasted deprecation and sunset notices — emails, changelog entries, docs pages — plus the endpoints and API versions you actually call
tools.hands_back: A dated sunset timeline — every called endpoint and version with its sunset date and days remaining — and a migration priority list ordered by deadline and how much you call it; anything with no notice is marked UNCONFIRMED, never safe

tools.name: J-Dawgs API Endpoint Reality Checker™
tools.description: Grades planned API calls against the API's own spec before any of them run: each call marked EXISTS, WRONG METHOD, INVENTED PATH (with the closest real endpoint suggested), DEPRECATED, or MISSING REQUIRED PARAMS — so the plan stops hallucinating endpoints before the first 404.
tools.takes_in: The planned API calls — method and path, with any parameters — plus the API's own spec: an OpenAPI document or the endpoint list it publishes
tools.hands_back: A grade per planned call — EXISTS, WRONG METHOD, INVENTED PATH with the closest real endpoint named, DEPRECATED, or MISSING REQUIRED PARAMS — and the corrected call list

tools.name: J-Dawgs API Schema Drift Detector™
tools.description: Paste the response shape your agent was built against and the JSON the API just returned — it compares them field by field and sorts the breaking drift from the harmless additions.
tools.takes_in: Two shapes: the API response shape your agent was built against, and the JSON the API just returned
tools.hands_back: A per-field findings table that separates BREAKING drift — missing fields, type changes, enum violations, suspected restructures — from harmless ADDITIVE changes, plus a plain-language fix list

tools.name: J-Dawgs Argument Provenance Checker™
tools.description: Paste your source context and planned tool calls; every argument value is classified Found in source / Derived (derivation shown) / Transformed / Invented, with invented sensitive arguments (email, amount, ID, date) escalated and a cleaned call with invented values stripped.
tools.takes_in: Your source context — the text the call is supposed to be built from — plus the planned tool calls with their argument values
tools.hands_back: Every argument value classified Found in source / Derived (with the derivation shown) / Transformed / Invented, invented sensitive arguments — email, amount, ID, date — escalated, and a cleaned call with the invented values stripped

tools.name: J-Dawgs Arithmetic & Totals Auditor™
tools.description: Paste a draft report, invoice, or quote; every written equation, line-item total, subtotal-plus-tax chain, and percentage claim in it is recomputed with real arithmetic and flagged where the draft's math does not hold.
tools.takes_in: A draft with numbers in it — a report, invoice, quote, or estimate carrying written equations, line items, totals, tax chains, or percentage claims
tools.hands_back: Every equation, line-item total, subtotal-plus-tax chain, and percentage claim recomputed with real arithmetic — each flagged where the draft's math does not hold, with the draft figure, the recomputed figure, and the difference

tools.name: J-Dawgs Blank Page Diagnostician™
tools.description: Blank page, no error, no clue? Paste the page URL and its HTML/JS source and get a ranked diagnosis — missing mount node, unparseable embedded JSON, a script running before its DOM node, unbalanced code, blocking head scripts — each finding with the exact evidence and the concrete fix, plus a clean bill of what passed. For Muse share links it leads with the honest answer: that white screen is Muse's loading shell, not a broken page.
tools.takes_in: A page URL plus the page's HTML/JS source, pasted — the markup and scripts behind the blank page
tools.hands_back: A ranked diagnosis — every likely cause with the exact evidence from the source and the concrete fix for each — plus a clean bill listing what passed; for Muse share links, the honest first answer that the white screen is Muse's loading shell, not a broken page

tools.name: J-Dawgs Blocker Triage & Minimal Ask Builder™
tools.description: Paste a plan that's stuck and find out which blockers are really the human's problem — each one classified with the signal words shown, and everything that genuinely needs the human folded into one short ask instead of a pile of interruptions.
tools.takes_in: A blocked plan — the plan text with its blockers, pasted as-is
tools.hands_back: Every blocker classified SELF-SERVE, NEEDS-HUMAN-JUDGMENT, NEEDS-HUMAN-HANDS, EXTERNAL-WAIT, or NOT-A-BLOCKER with the signal words that decided it, an APPROVAL OVERLOAD flag when more than 3 items head to the human, and one copyable Minimal Ask containing only the human items, credential values stripped

tools.name: J-Dawgs Browser Selector Fragility Auditor™
tools.description: Scores every locator and fixed wait in Playwright/Puppeteer/Selenium code for fragility — absolute XPath, generated classes, nth-child, sleeps — and produces a worst-first rewrite plan toward resilient locators.
tools.takes_in: Browser automation code — Playwright, Puppeteer, or Selenium — with the locators, selectors, and waits it uses to find and drive page elements
tools.hands_back: A fragility score for every locator and fixed wait in the code, ranked worst-first, with the brittle pattern named for each and a rewrite plan toward resilient locators — roles, labels, and test IDs instead of paths and positions

tools.name: J-Dawgs Cache Key Collision & Tenant-Leak Auditor™
tools.description: A cache key is a trust boundary nobody audits: paste your key patterns and sample keys and get collisions flagged, shared-cache keys with no tenant scoping named, raw user input sitting in keys called out, and TTL risks listed — before one tenant reads another tenant's data.
tools.takes_in: Your cache key patterns plus sample keys as actually written — and which caches are shared between tenants
tools.hands_back: Every collision flagged with the keys involved, shared-cache keys missing tenant scoping named as tenant-leak risks, raw user input in keys called out, and TTL risks listed — each with the fix

tools.name: J-Dawgs Calendar Invite Integrity Auditor™
tools.description: Paste an .ics calendar file and get it audited before anyone imports it: missing UID or DTSTAMP, floating times with no timezone, undefined TZIDs, duplicate UIDs, open-ended RRULEs, and overlapping events — ending in one import verdict. The file you paste is all it reads.
tools.takes_in: A pasted .ics (iCalendar) file — a single invite or a whole calendar export
tools.hands_back: One import verdict — IMPORT, FIX FIRST, or DO NOT IMPORT — with every defect named by event: missing UID or DTSTAMP, floating times, undefined TZIDs, duplicate UIDs, open-ended RRULEs, and overlapping events

tools.name: J-Dawgs Chunk Boundary Damage Bench™
tools.description: Splitters cut and stay silent about the damage; this bench shows it before a single embedding is bought: paste a document, run two chunking strategies side by side, and see every chunk with boundary-damage flags (mid-sentence cuts, broken code fences, orphaned headings, severed procedures, tiny fragments), size spread, and a verdict per strategy.
tools.takes_in: A document to be chunked for embedding or retrieval — plus the chunk size and overlap to test, or two named strategies to compare
tools.hands_back: Both chunk sets side by side: every chunk with its boundary-damage flags, the size spread per strategy, and a verdict per strategy — which one damages this document less, and where

tools.name: J-Dawgs Citation Grounding Checker™
tools.description: Catches vibe citing: paste each claim with its citation and source excerpt, and it checks the excerpt actually carries the claim — verbatim quotes, numbers, names, placeholder DOIs. It checks the excerpt you paste; it does not browse the web.
tools.takes_in: Each claim with its citation and the source excerpt it rests on
tools.hands_back: A check of whether the excerpt actually carries the claim — verbatim quotes, numbers, and names verified against it, and placeholder DOIs flagged; it checks the excerpt you paste and does not browse the web

tools.name: J-Dawgs Claim Checker™
tools.description: Paste a claim and the source text it supposedly comes from. It compares them in the browser and tells you whether the source actually supports the claim — now with a batch mode that scores many claims in one pass, each claim graded for evidence strength: STRONG, WEAK, or NONE. $0.50 per use.
tools.takes_in: A claim, plus the source text it supposedly comes from
tools.hands_back: Supported, Partially supported, Not found in source, or Contradicted — with a detail breakdown, highlighted evidence quotes, and found / missing lists, plus a report you can copy or download

tools.name: J-Dawgs Commitment Date & SLA Promise Auditor™
tools.description: Extracts every date and deadline promise from a draft message and checks each against today, lead time, business days, and blackout dates — past dates, weekend promises, and vague 'soon' commitments flagged before the message goes out.
tools.takes_in: A draft message containing date or deadline commitments, today's date, and — where they apply — the required lead time, business-day rules, and blackout dates
tools.hands_back: Every promise extracted and checked one by one: past dates, weekend and blackout-date promises, lead-time violations, and vague commitments like ‘soon’, each flagged with the quoted wording and a corrected date or phrasing

tools.name: J-Dawgs Compaction Loss Auditor™
tools.description: Compaction keeps the plot and loses the specifics — this catches the specifics before you continue on a summary you can't trust. Compares an agent's original notes against the compacted summary that replaced them: extracts numbers, dates, names, decisions and constraints from the original, classifies each as KEPT, SOFTENED or LOST, and returns a copyable rescue list of everything compaction dropped.
tools.takes_in: An agent's original notes, plus the compacted summary that replaced them — both pasted as-is
tools.hands_back: Every number, date, name, decision and constraint from the original classified as KEPT, SOFTENED or LOST, plus a copyable rescue list of everything compaction dropped

tools.name: J-Dawgs Connector Credential & Egress Verifier™
tools.description: Paste a failed connector or API call's error output plus its setup facts; the failure is classified — placeholder token reaching the provider unswapped, missing credential, placement mismatch, unregistered host, insufficient key scope, malformed or masked credential, account not activated — and you get the fix checklist for that exact failure, plus a preflight list for setting the connector up right the first time.
tools.takes_in: The error output of a failed connector or API call — its HTTP status and error body — plus the setup facts: the auth scheme, where the credential was placed, and whether the provider host was registered for the connector
tools.hands_back: One named diagnosis with the evidence quoted from the pasted error, an ordered fix checklist specific to that failure class, and a preflight checklist for first-time connector setup

tools.name: J-Dawgs Consent Scope Auditor™
tools.description: Extracts what a user actually granted, denied, or time-boxed from a pasted history and checks each planned action against it — silence is never consent, and scope creep is named.
tools.takes_in: A pasted history of what the user said — the grants, denials, and time-boxes in their own words — plus the actions you plan to take
tools.hands_back: Each planned action marked covered, denied, time-boxed (with the window), or never granted — with scope creep named where a plan stretches a grant past what was said

tools.name: J-Dawgs Container Build Safety Auditor™
tools.description: Install-first Dockerfile linters stop at per-line style rules; ours also grades the runtime posture (root user, secrets in build args, remote-script pipes) and returns one ship verdict with a fix list — no install.
tools.takes_in: A pasted Dockerfile — plus the build args and the .dockerignore, if you have them
tools.hands_back: One ship verdict — SHIP, FIX FIRST, or DO NOT SHIP — with every finding graded, the runtime posture scored, and a fix list in the order to work it

tools.name: J-Dawgs Context Budget Planner™
tools.description: Plan a prompt against a finite context window: zone-by-zone token estimates, a FITS / TIGHT / OVER BUDGET verdict, and a trim plan in priority order.
tools.takes_in: A prompt in zones — system text, instructions, examples, documents, history — plus the context window size it has to fit
tools.hands_back: A token estimate for each zone, the total against the window, a FITS / TIGHT / OVER BUDGET verdict, and a prioritized trim plan naming what to cut first

tools.name: J-Dawgs Correction Persistence Checker™
tools.description: Checks a mid-task correction log against the final output and any parallel worker outputs — every correction marked APPLIED, REVERTED (the old value still standing, quoted), or DID NOT SPREAD — with a copyable fix list for everything that didn't stick.
tools.takes_in: The mid-task correction log — what was corrected, from what, to what — plus the final output and, where they exist, the parallel worker outputs
tools.hands_back: A verdict per correction — APPLIED, REVERTED with the old value quoted where it still stands, or DID NOT SPREAD — and a copyable fix list for everything that didn't stick

tools.name: J-Dawgs Cron Explainer™
tools.description: Paste a cron expression, get plain words and a next-5-runs preview — now with timezone selection and DST gap/overlap warnings on the runs ahead, warnings for the traps cron hides (day 29–31 skipped in short months, Feb 29 and leap years, the day-of-month/day-of-week OR rule, day-of-week 7, and schedules that fire very often), and a copyable summary in human and machine form. It now also has a Schedule Overlap Checker: paste two expressions and it lays both schedules over the next 7 days, naming every moment they collide.
tools.takes_in: A five-field cron expression, and the timezone to preview the runs in
tools.hands_back: Whether the expression is valid, a plain-words explanation of the schedule, and a preview of the next five runs in the timezone you select — with warnings where a run falls in a DST gap or a DST overlap, where day 29–31 is skipped in a short month, where Feb 29 waits for a leap year, where the day-of-month/day-of-week OR rule fires more often than intended, what day-of-week 7 means, and when a schedule fires very often — plus a copyable summary in human and machine form

tools.name: J-Dawgs Cross-Document Consistency Checker™
tools.description: Compares the labeled facts — money, dates, versions, status — across two or three documents and flags the mismatches side by side: the same fact stated differently in different places, with format-only differences normalized away so real disagreements stand out.
tools.takes_in: Two or three documents — drafts, listings, messages, specs — whose facts are supposed to agree
tools.hands_back: A side-by-side table of every shared labeled fact — money, dates, versions, status — with each mismatch flagged and both values quoted, and format-only differences marked as the same fact

tools.name: J-Dawgs Cross-Provider Strict Schema Fixer™
tools.description: Checks a pasted JSON Schema against the documented strict-mode subsets for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini, lists every violation with its path, and outputs a converted provider-ready schema — flagging oneOf, allOf, and recursive $ref as UNCONVERTIBLE instead of silently rewriting them.
tools.takes_in: A JSON Schema — plus the provider you are targeting: OpenAI, Anthropic, or Gemini strict mode
tools.hands_back: Every violation with its schema path, and a converted provider-ready schema — with anything that cannot be converted flagged UNCONVERTIBLE, never silently rewritten

tools.name: J-Dawgs CSV & Tabular Integrity Auditor™
tools.description: Audits a pasted CSV, TSV, or Markdown table before you trust it: quote-aware parsing with delimiter detection, ragged rows and duplicate headers flagged, per-column type profiling with type-drift cells named by row, mixed date formats and leading-zero loss called out, duplicate rows caught — and a CLEAN / USE WITH FIXES / DO NOT TRUST verdict with a fix checklist.
tools.takes_in: A table pasted as text — a CSV, TSV, or Markdown table an agent received from anywhere — exactly as it arrived, delimiters, quotes, and ragged edges included
tools.hands_back: A full integrity audit: the parse report (delimiter detected, quoting handled), ragged-row and duplicate-header flags, a per-column type profile with every type-drift cell named by row, mixed date-format detection, leading-zero loss risks, duplicate and near-duplicate rows, and a CLEAN / USE WITH FIXES / DO NOT TRUST verdict with a fix checklist

tools.name: J-Dawgs Curl Command Safety & Translation Bench™
tools.description: Paste a curl command and get it audited before anyone runs it — the -k flag that switches off certificate checks, credentials embedded in the URL or headers, auth sent over plain http — then translated: the same request as fetch() code, and a cleaned-up curl with placeholders where the secrets were. The command is never run.
tools.takes_in: One curl command, pasted as text — flags, headers, URL, and body exactly as copied
tools.hands_back: Every dangerous flag and embedded secret named with the risk, the same request translated to fetch() code, and a cleaned curl with placeholders in place of the credentials — the command itself never runs

tools.name: J-Dawgs Data Converter™
tools.description: Convert between JSON, CSV, Markdown tables, and YAML — right in the browser: format auto-detect graded CERTAIN, LIKELY, or GUESS with the evidence shown, a round-trip fidelity check that names every lossy change, and a per-field type report. It now makes zero external requests — system fonts only, so nothing is fetched to run it. It now also supports JSON Lines / NDJSON in and out and warns on duplicate JSON keys that parsers silently drop. Free.
tools.takes_in: Data in JSON, CSV, a Markdown table, YAML, or JSON Lines / NDJSON — format auto-detected
tools.hands_back: The same data in the format you asked for, ready to copy or download; a round-trip fidelity check naming every lossy change the conversion made; a per-field type report; for broken JSON, the fixed version plus a list of exactly what changed; for schema checks, per-field errors

tools.name: J-Dawgs Data Retention & Deletion Proof Checker™
tools.description: Audits a deletion/retention log against your stated policy — overdue keeps, deletions without proof, unaccounted backup copies — and writes a completion statement that never claims more than the log proves.
tools.takes_in: Your stated retention and deletion policy, plus the deletion/retention log — what was kept, what was deleted, when, and what proof each deletion carries
tools.hands_back: Every log line checked against the policy: overdue keeps past their retention limit, deletions recorded without proof, and backup copies the log never accounts for — plus a completion statement that claims exactly what the log proves and no more

tools.name: J-Dawgs Dead-Letter Replay Safety Checker™
tools.description: Replay-all is how a dead-letter queue turns one bad job into a hundred: paste a dead-letter or failed-job export before anything replays and get every job classified POISON, DUPLICATE-RISK, STALE, or SAFE — duplicate ids and duplicate payloads detected — plus a safe replay plan. It never connects to a queue and never replays anything.
tools.takes_in: A dead-letter or failed-job export — the failed jobs as exported: ids, payloads, attempt counts, error messages, and timestamps
tools.hands_back: Every job classified POISON, DUPLICATE-RISK, STALE, or SAFE with the reason shown, duplicate ids and duplicate payloads named, and a safe replay plan — what replays, what quarantines, and in what order

tools.name: J-Dawgs Dependency & Lockfile Conflict Auditor™
tools.description: Audits a manifest against its lockfile and install error log with real semver math: ranges the lock doesn't satisfy, duplicate majors, peer-dependency conflicts, and unpinned ranges — with quoted evidence and a fix plan before you burn hours on install hell.
tools.takes_in: A dependency manifest (package.json, requirements.txt, or the like), its lockfile, and — where you have one — the install error log
tools.hands_back: A conflict report with the offending lines quoted as evidence — ranges the lock doesn't satisfy, duplicate majors, peer-dependency conflicts, and unpinned ranges — plus a fix plan in the order to apply it

tools.name: J-Dawgs DNS Record Pre-Flight Auditor™
tools.description: Paste the DNS records you're about to publish and get them audited as a set before they go live: duplicate SPF records and a permissive +all, MX records with no DMARC, a CNAME colliding with other records at the same name, and targets that dangle inside the pasted set. It audits the pasted records only — no live lookups.
tools.takes_in: The DNS records you are about to publish, pasted as a set — A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT (SPF/DMARC), and the rest, as written
tools.hands_back: Every conflict and hazard in the set named — duplicate or permissive SPF, MX without DMARC, CNAME collisions, dangling targets — each with the record it sits on and the fix, before anything goes live

tools.name: J-Dawgs Email Header & Delivery-Auth Auditor™
tools.description: Paste a message's full headers and get its delivery authentication audited: the SPF, DKIM, and DMARC results as recorded, whether the From, Return-Path, and DKIM domains actually align, classic spoof patterns, and the timing across the Received hops — ending in one trust verdict. It reads the headers you paste; it runs no DNS checks.
tools.takes_in: A message's full raw headers, pasted as received — Authentication-Results, From, Return-Path, DKIM-Signature, and the Received chain
tools.hands_back: The recorded SPF, DKIM, and DMARC results, the alignment verdict for From vs. Return-Path vs. DKIM domain, any spoof patterns named, the Received-hop timeline with its timing gaps, and one trust verdict

tools.name: J-Dawgs Env & Config Drift Auditor™
tools.description: Cross-checks your actual .env, your .env.example, and the variables your code and CI actually reference: missing, undocumented, placeholder, empty, duplicate, and near-miss-named variables (FEED_TOKEN vs FEED_TOKEN_V2) caught before deploy, with a corrected template and every secret value masked.
tools.takes_in: Your actual .env, your .env.example template, and — where you have them — pasted code or CI config showing which variables get referenced
tools.hands_back: A drift report naming every missing, undocumented, placeholder, empty, duplicate, and near-miss-named variable, plus a corrected .env.example template — with every secret value masked everywhere it appears

tools.name: J-Dawgs Eval Assertion Scorecard™
tools.description: Paste captured model outputs, get a deterministic assertion scorecard — required and forbidden phrases, a credential scan, JSON validity and required keys, length and cost bands — plus a red-team coverage audit listing which of 10 risk categories your test set never touches.
tools.takes_in: Captured model outputs — the responses as they actually came back — plus the assertions to score them against: required and forbidden phrases, required JSON keys, and length or cost bands
tools.hands_back: A deterministic assertion scorecard — every output scored pass or fail on every assertion, with the evidence shown — plus a red-team coverage audit naming which of the 10 risk categories your test set never touches

tools.name: J-Dawgs Eval Case Forge™
tools.description: Describe an agent's task, its allowed and forbidden tools, and the ways it has failed before — get back a structured eval suite that tests the happy path and the ugly ones, each case scored against a rubric with must-pass safety gates.
tools.takes_in: An agent's task description, its allowed and forbidden tools, and its past failures
tools.hands_back: A structured eval suite — happy, missing-info, ambiguous, tool-error, forbidden-action, injection, and messy-input cases, plus labeled regression cases built from the past failures — each with a 0–5 correctness / trajectory / safety rubric and must-pass safety gates, coverage warnings, and export as JSON plus a checklist

tools.name: J-Dawgs Example-Data Leak Detector™
tools.description: Scans a draft or dataset for placeholder and example data that survived into the real thing — example.com addresses, 555 phone numbers, lorem ipsum, TODO markers, dummy keys — each find classified CERTAIN, LIKELY, or REVIEW before it ships as real.
tools.takes_in: A draft document, a dataset, a config, or listing copy that is about to ship as real
tools.hands_back: Every placeholder-looking find with its location and the text quoted, classified CERTAIN, LIKELY, or REVIEW — plus a clean bill for the categories where nothing was found

tools.name: J-Dawgs Feature Flag & Rollout Safety Auditor™
tools.description: Audits a feature-flag config before it ships: 100% production rollouts with no kill switch, conflicting duplicate flags, missing owners, stale flags past their review date, and retire candidates.
tools.takes_in: A feature-flag configuration — flag names, rollout percentages, environments, owners, and review or expiry dates — before it ships
tools.hands_back: An audit report flagging the dangerous shapes — full rollouts with no kill switch, conflicting duplicates, missing owners, stale flags, and retire candidates — each with the fix

tools.name: J-Dawgs Feed Validity & Freshness Auditor™
tools.description: Paste an RSS or Atom feed and get it audited before you publish: duplicate guids, future-dated items, missing dates, relative links, out-of-order items, and a freshness summary of how stale the feed has gone. It never fetches the feed — the XML you paste is all it reads.
tools.takes_in: A pasted RSS or Atom feed — the full XML, exactly as it would be published
tools.hands_back: A publish verdict with every defect named — duplicate guids, future dates, missing dates, relative links, out-of-order items — plus a freshness summary: the newest item, the oldest item, and the longest gap between posts

tools.name: J-Dawgs File Operation Sandbox & Path Guard™
tools.description: Audits a planned list of agent file operations against allowed folders before anything runs: normalizes paths, flags traversal that resolves outside the root, sensitive paths (.env, .ssh, credentials, keys), absolute escapes, and bulk-delete blast radius — with per-operation verdicts and a rewritten safer plan.
tools.takes_in: A planned list of file operations — reads, writes, moves, and deletes, with the exact path each one will touch — plus the allowed root folders the agent is supposed to stay inside
tools.hands_back: A verdict for every operation — ALLOWED, FLAGGED, or BLOCKED — with the normalized path and the rule it tripped, a blast-radius read on bulk deletes, and a rewritten safer plan that keeps the allowed work and replaces the escapes

tools.name: J-Dawgs GitHub Actions Workflow Safety Auditor™
tools.description: Install-first workflow linters stop at syntax; ours audits a pasted GitHub Actions workflow in the browser — expression mistakes, permission excess, unpinned actions, deprecated versions — and returns one verdict plus a fix list.
tools.takes_in: A GitHub Actions workflow file, pasted as YAML — the whole workflow, triggers, jobs, permissions, and steps as written
tools.hands_back: One verdict on the workflow, plus a fix list: every expression mistake, every permission broader than the job needs, every action pinned to a moving tag instead of a commit, and every deprecated action version — each named with where it sits

tools.name: J-Dawgs Goal Drift & Termination Checker™
tools.description: Compares an agent's original goal and done criteria against its finished run transcript — every criterion marked MET, PARTIAL, or NO EVIDENCE with the evidence lines quoted, scope creep and drift flagged, and a termination verdict: stopped early, continued past done, drifted, or done cleanly.
tools.takes_in: The agent's original goal and done criteria, plus the finished run's transcript — the tool calls, outputs, and final answer
tools.hands_back: A per-criterion ledger — MET, PARTIAL, or NO EVIDENCE, each with the transcript lines quoted as evidence — scope-creep and drift flags, and one termination verdict: stopped early, continued past done, drifted, or done cleanly

tools.name: J-Dawgs Handoff Read-Back Checker™
tools.description: Handoff tools pack the brief; ours verifies the receiver's read-back — every blocker, do-not-redo item, and figure marked CONFIRMED, DISTORTED, or MISSING before work resumes.
tools.takes_in: The original handoff brief plus the receiver's read-back of it — what the receiving agent says it understood, in its own words
tools.hands_back: Every blocker, do-not-redo item, and figure from the brief marked CONFIRMED, DISTORTED, or MISSING in the read-back — with the distorted wording quoted side by side, so the gap is fixed before work resumes

tools.name: J-Dawgs HTTP Cache Freshness Auditor™
tools.description: Paste a response's headers and get the freshness math step by step — lifetime vs. age, every Cache-Control directive explained, and a verdict on whether the data may be presented as live.
tools.takes_in: One response's headers as received — Date, Age, Cache-Control, Expires, ETag, Last-Modified — and the moment the data was fetched
tools.hands_back: The freshness math step by step — freshness lifetime vs. current age — every Cache-Control directive explained in plain words, and a verdict: FRESH, STALE, or NEVER PRESENTABLE AS LIVE

tools.name: J-Dawgs Idempotency & Duplicate-Action Guard™
tools.description: Paste an agent action log: it finds the actions that ran twice — exact and near duplicates, idempotency keys reused where they shouldn't be, writes sent with no key at all, and retries fired after timeouts — and hands back a reconcile-first safe-retry plan.
tools.takes_in: An agent action log, pasted as-is — the actions in order, their idempotency keys where present, and their outcomes, timeouts included
tools.hands_back: Every exact and near duplicate flagged, idempotency-key reuse bugs and keyless writes listed, unsafe retries after timeouts called out, and a reconcile-first safe-retry plan for each case

tools.name: J-Dawgs Ignore-Rule & Publish-Safety Auditor™
tools.description: Single-path ignore checkers stop at one file and one yes/no; ours tests a whole file list at once, names the exact rule that decided each path, and flags sensitive files that would still ship.
tools.takes_in: Your ignore rules (.gitignore and friends) plus the full list of file paths about to ship — the whole tree at once, not one file at a time
tools.hands_back: Every path marked ignored or shipping, the exact rule — file and line — that decided it, and the sensitive files (.env, keys, credentials) that would still ship flagged by name

tools.name: J-Dawgs Instruction Conflict Scanner™
tools.description: Paste your system instructions, the user task, and untrusted content — it scans only the untrusted content for planted directives and rates each one it finds.
tools.takes_in: Three pastes: your system instructions, the user task, and the untrusted content — a tool result, a fetched page, or file text
tools.hands_back: Every planted directive found in the untrusted content, rated CRITICAL, HIGH, or MEDIUM, each with the exact line quoted and a recommended action

tools.name: J-Dawgs Instruction Retention & Coverage Auditor™
tools.description: Paste the original instructions and the agent's final output; get a per-instruction verdict — addressed, partial, no evidence found, or guardrail violated — with the evidence lines quoted and a ready-to-send re-issue list for whatever was dropped.
tools.takes_in: The original instructions given to an agent, and the agent's final output
tools.hands_back: A verdict for every instruction — addressed, partial, no evidence found, or guardrail violated — with the evidence lines from the output quoted behind each verdict, plus a ready-to-send re-issue list covering whatever was dropped

tools.name: J-Dawgs Invisible Character & Unicode Trap Sweeper™
tools.description: Scans pasted text and tool output codepoint by codepoint for zero-width characters, bidi overrides, homoglyph lookalike words, and Unicode tag characters — decoding any hidden tag-character message it finds — and returns a cleaned copy.
tools.takes_in: Pasted text or tool output exactly as received — web copy, documents, logs, file contents, anything about to enter the agent's context or be quoted onward
tools.hands_back: A codepoint-by-codepoint findings list — every invisible or deceptive character named by codepoint and position, any hidden tag-character message decoded into plain sight, homoglyph lookalike words flagged — plus a cleaned copy of the text with the traps removed and the visible words unchanged

tools.name: J-Dawgs Irreversible Action Receipt & Rollback Planner™
tools.description: Turns planned agent actions into reversibility-checked receipts with rollback steps before anything irreversible runs: flags production + irreversible STOPs and vague-target blast radius.
tools.takes_in: The actions an agent is about to take, as planned — what each one does, what it acts on, and whether the target is production, a sandbox, or unstated
tools.hands_back: One receipt per action — REVERSIBLE, REVERSIBLE WITH STEPS, IRREVERSIBLE, or STOP — with the rollback steps for everything recoverable, and a blast-radius warning wherever the target is too vague to bound

tools.name: J-Dawgs Issue Inbox Deduper & Triage Bench™
tools.description: Paste an issue list and get near-duplicate clusters with a suggested canonical item for each, plus a transparent triage ranking that shows the exact signal words behind every score — no black-box priority.
tools.takes_in: An issue list — titles and descriptions as they arrived, one issue per line or pasted as a block
tools.hands_back: Near-duplicate clusters with a suggested canonical item for each cluster, and a triage ranking of the canonical issues with the exact signal words behind every score shown

tools.name: J-Dawgs JSON Damage Receipt™
tools.description: Forensics on repaired or truncated JSON: where it was cut, and which fields are intact, completed, guessed, or missing. It does not repair — the Almost-JSON Repair Bench fixes it; this proves what the fix changed.
tools.takes_in: The damaged JSON as it arrived — plus, when you have it, the repaired version to compare it against
tools.hands_back: A damage receipt: where the JSON was cut, and every field classified intact, completed, guessed, or missing — the proof of what a repair changed

tools.name: J-Dawgs JWT Safety Auditor™
tools.description: Paste a JSON Web Token and get it decoded and audited in the browser: alg=none and other dangerous algorithm choices, a missing or blown expiry, an over-long lifetime, and sensitive claims riding in the payload — plus a redacted, share-safe version of the token. It cannot verify the signature, and says so.
tools.takes_in: One JSON Web Token, pasted as text — header, payload, and signature segments as issued
tools.hands_back: The decoded header and payload in plain words, every audit finding — algorithm, expiry, lifetime, sensitive claims — and a redacted share-safe version of the token with the signature and sensitive claims masked

tools.name: J-Dawgs Listing Claims Auditor™
tools.description: Paste listing copy, get every price and fee claim pulled into one clean table — contradictions flagged.
tools.takes_in: Listing or marketing copy — a product listing, a sales page, an ad
tools.hands_back: Every price and fee claim extracted with the sentence it came from, a clean price table, flagged contradictions, and ambiguous claims marked as needing a human decision

tools.name: J-Dawgs Log Flood & First-Failure Triage Bench™
tools.description: Compresses a huge log dump into the first real failure with its stack frames: distinct error clusters ranked by first appearance, later errors labeled likely fallout, duplicate and noise stats, and a terse agent-ready summary with raw-vs-summary token estimates.
tools.takes_in: A log dump as text — the bigger and messier the better: full runs, stack traces, retries, and all the noise around them
tools.hands_back: The first real failure with its stack frames, the distinct error clusters ranked by first appearance with later errors labeled LIKELY FALLOUT, duplicate and noise statistics, and a terse agent-ready summary with raw-vs-summary token estimates

tools.name: J-Dawgs Markdown Anchor & Link Integrity Auditor™
tools.description: Recomputes GitHub's heading anchors for a pasted Markdown doc and checks every in-page link, reference link, duplicate heading, and image alt text — with line numbers and fix suggestions for each break.
tools.takes_in: A Markdown document pasted in full — README, guide, or docs page — exactly as it will be published
tools.hands_back: A findings list with a line number for every problem: in-page links pointing at anchors no heading produces, reference links defined but never used or used but never defined, duplicate headings that collide on one anchor, and images with missing or empty alt text — each with the fix to apply

tools.name: J-Dawgs MCP Permission Least-Privilege Auditor™
tools.description: Paste an MCP config before you connect it: it scores every server's blast radius, flags write/delete/execute tools, broad paths and shared credentials (the toxic-flow pattern), and outputs a read-only allowlist. Env values are never shown — key names only.
tools.takes_in: An MCP config, pasted before you connect it
tools.hands_back: A blast-radius score for every server, flags on write/delete/execute tools, broad paths and shared credentials, and a read-only allowlist; env values are never shown — key names only

tools.name: J-Dawgs MCP Session Transcript Diagnostician™
tools.description: Decodes a pasted captured MCP JSON-RPC session transcript into a timeline with a handshake check, plain-language error-code explanations, and malformed lines named by number — plus an optional two-session tool-schema drift diff. It never connects to a server.
tools.takes_in: A captured MCP session transcript — the JSON-RPC lines as logged — plus, optionally, a second session's transcript to diff tool schemas against
tools.hands_back: A timeline of the session with the handshake checked, every error code explained in plain language, malformed lines named by line number — and, with a second session, a tool-schema drift diff

tools.name: J-Dawgs Memory Staleness Auditor™
tools.description: Paste an agent's memory notes and find what's gone stale — conflicting values, corrections buried under the lines they replaced, duplicates, and facts too old to trust — sorted into what stands, what retires, and what needs checking.
tools.takes_in: An agent's memory notes, pasted as text — dated or not, tidy or not
tools.hands_back: A current-state table of the facts as they now stand, a retire list of superseded and duplicate lines, and a verify list of undated or aged-out facts that need checking before they're trusted

tools.name: J-Dawgs Model Fallback Chain Safety Checker™
tools.description: A fallback chain fails silently: the backup model answers, but something the workload needed is gone. Paste your fallback chain and the capabilities the workload requires, and this checker walks it hop by hop against an editable, date-stamped on-page snapshot table — never a live lookup — naming every silent capability drop at every hop.
tools.takes_in: Your model fallback chain in order, plus the capabilities the workload requires — context size, tool calling, vision, structured output, and the rest
tools.hands_back: A hop-by-hop walk of the chain: at every fallback, exactly which required capabilities drop and which survive, and the first hop where the workload breaks — checked against the editable, date-stamped snapshot table, never a live lookup

tools.name: J-Dawgs Multi-Agent Merge Conflict Checker™
tools.description: Compares 2–4 parallel sub-agent reports key by key before anyone merges them: AGREED, CONFLICT (every value shown with its source), SINGLE-SOURCE, and DUPLICATE WORK, plus a decision-clash pass for opposing go/no-go calls; the merge sheet lists DECISION NEEDED lines and never picks a winner itself.
tools.takes_in: 2–4 parallel sub-agent reports on the same task, pasted as-is, each labeled with which agent produced it
tools.hands_back: A merge sheet comparing the reports key by key — AGREED, CONFLICT with every value shown alongside its source, SINGLE-SOURCE, and DUPLICATE WORK — plus a decision-clash pass over opposing go/no-go calls and DECISION NEEDED lines for everything a human or lead agent must settle; it never picks a winner itself

tools.name: J-Dawgs Open-Loop & Abandoned-Thread Detector™
tools.description: Scans a transcript or log for the loops that were opened and never closed — questions never answered, promises never kept, tasks deferred and forgotten, decisions left hanging — each one with its quoted evidence and a closing checklist to work through.
tools.takes_in: A run transcript, a chat log, or a work log — plus, optionally, the closing messages or outputs where loops would have been closed
tools.hands_back: Every open loop found, typed as QUESTION, PROMISE, DEFERRED TASK, or DECISION, with the quoted line that opened it and the evidence it was never closed — plus a closing checklist

tools.name: J-Dawgs OpenAPI Example & Breaking-Change Auditor™
tools.description: Paste an old and a new OpenAPI document and get one breaking-change verdict, every breaking change located, and every embedded example validated against its own schema — install-first linters stop at style rules; this one also checks the examples.
tools.takes_in: Two OpenAPI documents — the previous version and the new version, pasted as YAML or JSON
tools.hands_back: One breaking-change verdict for the pair, every breaking change located by path and operation, and every embedded example in both documents validated against its own schema — the examples that fail their own schema named

tools.name: J-Dawgs Outbound Message Recipient & Disclosure Guard™
tools.description: Pre-flights an outbound message before it is sent: compares intended vs actual recipients, flags external domains under an internal-only audience, sensitive content classes headed outside, internal-only terms, and attachment mismatches — and rules SAFE TO SEND, REVIEW RECIPIENTS, or DO NOT SEND.
tools.takes_in: A draft outbound message, the audience it is intended for (for example internal-only), the actual recipient list — To, Cc, and Bcc — and the names of the files actually attached
tools.hands_back: A verdict — SAFE TO SEND, REVIEW RECIPIENTS, or DO NOT SEND — with every flag itemized: recipients outside the intended audience by domain, the sensitive content classes found in the text and where they are headed, internal-only terms quoted in place, and attachments mentioned but missing or attached but never mentioned

tools.name: J-Dawgs Outline Promise & Section Delivery Auditor™
tools.description: Paste a finished long document: promised sections from its outline and intro are aligned against the headings it actually delivered — missing, renumbered, and dangling 'Section N' references named before it ships.
tools.takes_in: A finished long document — the full text, with the sections its outline and introduction promise and the headings it actually delivered
tools.hands_back: The promised sections aligned against the delivered headings — every missing section, every renumbered section, and every dangling ‘Section N’ reference named, with the line that promised it

tools.name: J-Dawgs Package Hallucination & Slopsquat Risk Checker™
tools.description: Audits package.json, requirements.txt, install commands, and imports before install: typosquat near-misses named side by side, mashup names, unpinned versions, and git/URL installs flagged with a verify-before-install checklist — pattern checks only, it does not query a live registry.
tools.takes_in: A package.json or requirements.txt, a set of install commands an agent is about to run, or the import lines from generated code — whatever names the packages about to be installed
tools.hands_back: A per-package risk audit: typosquat near-misses named side by side with the well-known package they resemble, mashup names, unpinned versions, and git/URL installs, each with a verify-before-install checklist

tools.name: J-Dawgs Patch & Diff Safety Reviewer™
tools.description: Audits a pasted git diff before merge: test tampering and weakened assertions, secrets added (shown masked), CI/config witness editing, blast radius, sensitive files, sleep/retry fake fixes, and silent scope removal — ending in a merge-gate verdict and a copyable report.
tools.takes_in: A git diff, pasted as text — the patch exactly as it would be merged, headers and all
tools.hands_back: A merge-gate verdict — DO NOT MERGE, REVIEW CAREFULLY, or LOW RISK — with findings per category, every secret shown masked, a blast-radius read on the files touched, and a copyable report you can paste into the pull request

tools.name: J-Dawgs PII Redaction Consistency Checker™
tools.description: Checks whether personal data is redacted consistently through a whole document — a name masked in the body but visible in a footer is a CRITICAL leak — with a SAFE TO SHARE / DO NOT SHARE verdict and a fix list.
tools.takes_in: A document that has been redacted and is about to be shared — the full text, headers, footers, and all
tools.hands_back: A SAFE TO SHARE or DO NOT SHARE verdict, every place a redacted value still appears in the clear — quoted, with its location — and a fix list

tools.name: J-Dawgs Plan Dependency & Precondition Checker™
tools.description: Paste a multi-step agent plan and it builds the dependency graph: finds cycles, missing prerequisites, use-before-produce ordering errors, duplicate producers, orphan steps, and destructive steps with no backup covering them, then returns a corrected execution order and a READY / READY WITH FIXES / DO NOT RUN verdict.
tools.takes_in: A multi-step agent plan, pasted as-is — the steps in order, with what each step needs and what it produces where you know it
tools.hands_back: The plan's dependency graph with cycles, missing prerequisites, use-before-produce ordering errors, duplicate producers, orphan steps, and destructive steps with no backup covering them flagged, a corrected execution order, and a READY / READY WITH FIXES / DO NOT RUN verdict

tools.name: J-Dawgs Prompt Compression Loss Receipt™
tools.description: Learned compressors delete silently and the loss causes hallucination; this tool compresses deterministically only (duplicates, whitespace, checked boilerplate) and receipts every removed number, date, money amount, and named entity with its line number — and audits any original-vs-compressed pair for facts that disappeared.
tools.takes_in: A prompt to compress — or an original-and-compressed pair to audit
tools.hands_back: The deterministically compressed prompt plus a loss receipt: every removed number, date, money amount, and named entity with its line number — or, for a pair, the list of facts that disappeared

tools.name: J-Dawgs Prompt Regression Diff Checker™
tools.description: Paste the OLD and NEW versions of a system prompt and see exactly what the edit changed — a line diff by section, plus a guardrail scan that flags the constraints the new version lost or quietly weakened, before the new prompt ships.
tools.takes_in: Two versions of a system prompt — the OLD text and the NEW text — pasted side by side
tools.hands_back: A line diff grouped by section, a guardrail scan flagging LOST and WEAKENED constraints, every numbers-and-limits change and new permission, and one verdict — SHIP, REVIEW, or DO NOT SHIP YET — with a copyable report

tools.name: J-Dawgs Proof Photo Reuse & Metadata Checker™
tools.description: Fingerprint proof photos locally — SHA-256, dimensions, and JPEG EXIF capture time — and flag exact re-use of a photo across jobs, near-duplicates, and photos taken outside the claimed completion window. The photos never leave the device.
tools.takes_in: Proof photos from one or more jobs, opened locally in the browser, plus each job's claimed completion window
tools.hands_back: A fingerprint for every photo (SHA-256, dimensions, JPEG EXIF capture time), exact re-use across jobs flagged, near-duplicate pairs named, and any photo whose capture time falls outside its job's claimed completion window called out

tools.name: J-Dawgs Publish Accessibility Pre-Flight Auditor™
tools.description: Paste a page's HTML or Markdown before publishing and get a publish verdict with every missing or filename alt text, every generic link label, and every heading skip named with its line and a concrete fix.
tools.takes_in: A page's HTML or Markdown source, pasted before publishing
tools.hands_back: A publish verdict, and every finding with its line: missing or filename alt text, generic link labels like ‘click here’, and heading-level skips — each with a concrete fix

tools.name: J-Dawgs RAG Chunk & Retrieval Coverage Auditor™
tools.description: Separates retrieval failures from model failures: audits chunks for boundary splits, oversized chunks, duplicate / overlap waste, missing source metadata, and whether expected answer phrases are covered, split, or missing.
tools.takes_in: A RAG chunk set as produced by your chunker — the chunk texts with whatever metadata they carry — plus, optionally, the phrases a correct answer would need to contain
tools.hands_back: A chunk-by-chunk audit: boundary splits, oversized chunks, duplicate and overlap waste, and missing source metadata, plus a coverage table marking each expected answer phrase COVERED, SPLIT, or MISSING

tools.name: J-Dawgs Redirect Chain & Canonical Auditor™
tools.description: Paste a redirect graph — every hop as source, target, and status code — and get it audited before launch: loops, chains over 3 hops, https-to-http downgrades, and canonicals that disagree with where the chain actually lands. It never fetches a URL; the graph you paste is all it reads.
tools.takes_in: A pasted redirect graph: each redirect as source URL, target URL, and status code — plus the canonical URL each page declares, where known
tools.hands_back: A per-chain report — loops named hop by hop, every chain over 3 hops flagged with its length, every https-to-http downgrade, and every canonical that mismatches the chain's final URL — ending in one launch verdict

tools.name: J-Dawgs Regex ReDoS & Backtracking Safety Auditor™
tools.description: Audits a regex for catastrophic-backtracking and ReDoS risk — structural analysis of the pattern plus capped, timed near-miss probes — and suggests safer rewrites. The Regex Tester tests matches; this one tests safety.
tools.takes_in: A regular expression, the engine or flavor it runs in (JavaScript, PCRE, Python, and the like), and the kind of text it will be run against
tools.hands_back: A SAFE / RISKY / CATASTROPHIC verdict with the dangerous constructs named and located in the pattern, the probe evidence — near-miss inputs and how the time grew as they lengthened — and a safer rewrite for every flagged construct

tools.name: J-Dawgs Regex Tester™
tools.description: Test a pattern, see every match and capture group live — now with a batch test-case runner with expected match/no-match markers, a plain-English token-by-token pattern breakdown, and a lightweight catastrophic-backtracking caution that points to the ReDoS Safety Auditor for a full audit.
tools.takes_in: A regular expression, any flags, and the sample text to test it against
tools.hands_back: Every match highlighted live, with its position and capture groups, the pass or fail of every batch test case against its expected match or no-match, a plain-English breakdown of the pattern token by token, and a library of common patterns to start from

tools.name: J-Dawgs Retry & Rate-Limit Planner™
tools.description: Paste a run's error sequence and get a retry plan that knows the difference — 429s, transient failures, and errors that should never be retried — with the waits added up against your deadline before you spend them.
tools.takes_in: A run's error sequence — each error in order, with any Retry-After values — plus the task's deadline
tools.hands_back: Each error classified — 429 rate-limit, transient 5xx / timeout, or never-retry auth / validation — a retry plan with separate budgets per class, Retry-After honored exactly, and one verdict: FITS, OVER DEADLINE, or STOP NOW

tools.name: J-Dawgs Run Cost Auditor™
tools.description: Paste a finished run log and the rates you pay: it attributes cost step by step, ranks the waste (re-sent context, retry burn, cache misses), groups the run into a phase timeline and names its costliest step in one sentence, and hands back a hard-cap plan derived from your own log. Estimates from your rates only — not a bill.
tools.takes_in: A finished run log, plus the rates you pay
tools.hands_back: Cost attributed step by step, the waste ranked — re-sent context, retry burn, cache misses — the run grouped into a phase timeline with its costliest step named in one sentence, and a hard-cap plan derived from your own log; estimates from your rates only, not a bill

tools.name: J-Dawgs Schedule Time Pre-Flight Checker™
tools.description: Pre-flights a planned local date, time and IANA timezone before an agent schedules anything: catches nonexistent spring-forward (DST gap) times, ambiguous fall-back times with both UTC instants, weekday mismatches, and timezone-abbreviation traps, with a cross-zone conversion table.
tools.takes_in: A planned local date, time and IANA timezone — the exact moment you are about to schedule, plus any other zones you want it converted into
tools.hands_back: A pre-flight verdict on the moment: whether the local time exists at all, whether it is ambiguous (with both UTC instants spelled out), whether the weekday matches the date, and what any abbreviation really means — plus a cross-zone conversion table for the zones you named

tools.name: J-Dawgs Schema Inference Forge™
tools.description: Infers the shape a set of JSON records actually shares: paste multiple samples of the same record kind and get a recursive field census across all of them, type conflicts named by sample, sometimes-missing and always-null fields, enum candidates, array-item variance — and a copyable draft-07 JSON Schema with a STABLE SHAPE / SHAPE VARIES verdict.
tools.takes_in: Multiple JSON samples of the same record kind, pasted in sequence — several responses from one endpoint, several records from one export, several outputs from one model
tools.hands_back: A recursive field census across every sample: each field's presence count and types, type conflicts named by sample, sometimes-missing and always-null fields, enum candidates for low-variance string fields, array-item variance, and a copyable draft-07 JSON Schema whose required list holds only the fields present in every sample — plus a STABLE SHAPE / SHAPE VARIES verdict

tools.name: J-Dawgs Silent Result Triage Bench™
tools.description: Triages a batch of tool results against the expectations declared for them — EMPTY (an HTTP 200 that carried no data), PARTIAL, and SEMANTIC MISMATCH (the right shape holding the wrong kind of value) — and maps which downstream steps already consumed each bad result, before the agent trusts any of them.
tools.takes_in: A batch of tool results from one run, plus what each call was expected to return — the fields, counts, or values the plan depended on
tools.hands_back: Every result labeled EMPTY, PARTIAL, SEMANTIC MISMATCH, or SOUND with the evidence shown, plus a consumption map naming which downstream steps already used each bad result

tools.name: J-Dawgs Sitemap & Robots Agent-Access Auditor™
tools.description: Paste a robots.txt and a sitemap: per-agent access for ten well-known crawlers with the deciding rule quoted, sitemap entries your own rules block, and a fix list — nothing is ever fetched.
tools.takes_in: A robots.txt file and a sitemap, both pasted — the rules as written and the URLs the sitemap advertises
tools.hands_back: Per-agent access for ten well-known crawlers, each verdict with the deciding robots.txt rule quoted; every sitemap entry your own rules block, named; and a fix list — computed from the pasted text alone, nothing fetched

tools.name: J-Dawgs SQL Pre-Flight Guard™
tools.description: Audits SQL an agent is about to run before anything executes: splits and classifies each statement, blocks unscoped DELETE/UPDATE, DROP/TRUNCATE, and tautology WHERE clauses in Production mode, and returns a safer-plan checklist per flagged statement.
tools.takes_in: The SQL an agent is about to run — one statement or a whole script — plus the mode it will run in: production, staging, or unstated
tools.hands_back: A statement-by-statement audit: each statement classified, the dangerous ones flagged or blocked with the exact pattern that tripped the flag, and a safer-plan checklist per flagged statement — what to add, scope, or verify before it may run

tools.name: J-Dawgs Stale Evidence & Freshness Checker™
tools.description: Checks a draft answer against the retrieval dates and cache status of its sources: flags stale, undated, and cached-as-live evidence presented as current, labels each currency claim fresh or stale-backed, and inserts honest “as of” qualifiers — without changing any facts.
tools.takes_in: A draft answer, plus the sources behind it — each with the date it was retrieved and whether it came back live or served from cache
tools.hands_back: A label for every currency claim in the draft — FRESH or STALE-BACKED — with stale, undated, and cached-as-live evidence flagged, and the draft returned with honest “as of” qualifiers inserted and every fact left exactly as it was

tools.name: J-Dawgs Structured Output Conformance Bench™
tools.description: Batch-validates many LLM JSON outputs against one JSON Schema and classifies every failure by type (missing required, wrong type, enum miss, extra field, truncated, not JSON) with exact paths, a conformance rate, and the single most common fix needed. Classification only — it never invents values.
tools.takes_in: Many LLM JSON outputs, pasted as a batch, plus the one JSON Schema they were all supposed to follow
tools.hands_back: Every failure classified by type — missing required, wrong type, enum miss, extra field, truncated, not JSON — with the exact path of each failure, a conformance rate for the batch, and the single most common fix needed; classification only, it never invents values

tools.name: J-Dawgs Subagent Brief Stress-Tester™
tools.description: Paste a delegation brief before you hand it off: it scores the brief against 10 completeness elements, flags the drift risks and contradictions, and generates a tightened brief ready to send.
tools.takes_in: A delegation brief — the task text you are about to hand to a subagent, pasted as-is
tools.hands_back: A score against 10 completeness elements with each missing element named, the drift risks and contradictions flagged with the lines that cause them, and a tightened brief generated from yours, ready to send

tools.name: J-Dawgs Suppression & Opt-Out Honor Checker™
tools.description: Cross-checks a planned send list against suppression and opt-out lists — exact matches, case/plus-tag/phone-format variants, blocked domains, duplicates — and returns only the clean set with every removal accounted for.
tools.takes_in: A planned send list — email addresses and/or phone numbers — plus the suppression and opt-out lists it has to honor
tools.hands_back: Only the clean set, safe to send — plus a removal ledger naming every address taken out and the exact match or variant that removed it

tools.name: J-Dawgs Task Ambiguity Pre-Flight Checker™
tools.description: Agents guess when a task is underspecified, and the guess is where the damage happens: paste a task as received and get every gap flagged (missing done-definition, unresolved ‘the file’/‘them’ referents, vague ‘soon’/‘a few’, missing constraints, conflicting directives) with one ranked clarifying question per gap and a READY / ASSUMPTIONS LOGGED / ASK FIRST verdict.
tools.takes_in: A task exactly as received — the message, ticket, or instruction text, unedited
tools.hands_back: Every gap flagged by type with the offending words quoted, one ranked clarifying question per gap, and a READY / ASSUMPTIONS LOGGED / ASK FIRST verdict

tools.name: J-Dawgs Test Payload Forge™
tools.description: Forges test payload sets from a JSON Schema: a set of valid payloads that should pass, and a set of invalid ones that each break exactly one constraint — so a failing test tells you which rule fired, not just that something did.
tools.takes_in: A JSON Schema (draft-07) — plus, optionally, the fields or constraints you most want exercised
tools.hands_back: Two labeled payload sets: valid payloads that satisfy the schema, and invalid payloads that each violate exactly one named constraint — with the constraint each one breaks printed beside it

tools.name: J-Dawgs Tool Call Pre-Flight Checker™
tools.description: Check a proposed tool call against the tool's own JSON schema before it runs — tool name, required parameters, types, enums, and invented extras — and get corrected arguments back.
tools.takes_in: A proposed tool call — the tool name and its arguments — plus the tool's JSON schema
tools.hands_back: A check report: tool-name match, missing required parameters, argument-type and enum violations, invented parameters, placeholder-looking values flagged, a destructive-operation banner on send / write / delete tools, and suggested corrected arguments

tools.name: J-Dawgs Tool Description Collision Checker™
tools.description: Paste a set of tool definitions and find the pairs a model could mix up — every pair scored for description overlap, vague descriptions flagged, and the missing boundary lines drafted.
tools.takes_in: A set of tool definitions — JSON or plain text blocks — names and descriptions together
tools.hands_back: A pairwise overlap score for every pair of tools, flags on vague or name-echo descriptions, the missing boundary conditions for confusable pairs like list-vs-search and draft-vs-publish, and draft boundary rewrites labeled untested

tools.name: J-Dawgs Tool Distributor™
tools.description: Turn one tool into directory packets, social posts, and a feed entry agents can read.
tools.takes_in: One tool's details — name, URL, pitch, description, category, and price model
tools.hands_back: A filled directory submission packet, social announcement posts, a machine-readable feed entry, and an agent-facing blurb — all ready to copy or download

tools.name: J-Dawgs Tool Output Sanity Checker™
tools.description: Paste a chain of tool outputs and find the silent failures — empty results, ignored errors, truncated and malformed outputs, and shapes that drift between repeat calls — with one plain verdict at the end.
tools.takes_in: A pasted chain of agent tool outputs, in the order the steps ran
tools.hands_back: Per-step flags — EMPTY, ERROR-IGNORED, PARTIAL, MALFORMED, SHAPE-DRIFT — the first bad step named, and an overall verdict: TRUSTWORTHY, SUSPECT, or DO NOT PROCEED

tools.name: J-Dawgs Tool-Result Truncation & Pagination Checker™
tools.description: Proves a tool result is whole before the agent answers: detects silent truncation, count-vs-expected mismatches, and nextCursor / has_more pagination signals, and flags draft answers that claim “all” from partial data.
tools.takes_in: A tool result as returned — the items or text, any count or total the result or the call promised, and any pagination fields it carries — plus, optionally, the draft answer you are about to give from it
tools.hands_back: A wholeness verdict on the result — WHOLE, TRUNCATED, PAGINATED (more pages exist), or COUNT MISMATCH — with the exact signal each call rests on, plus flags on any draft-answer sentence that claims completeness the data doesn't support

tools.name: J-Dawgs Trademark Cost Calculator™
tools.description: Marks × classes × route = your USPTO filing total, line by line — now with a portfolio mode that plans up to 5 marks, per-mark fee lines, and a staged filing order.
tools.takes_in: Number of marks, classes per mark, the filing route, and any surcharges that apply
tools.hands_back: The USPTO filing total with a line-by-line breakdown of the fees and surcharges behind it

tools.name: J-Dawgs Transcript-to-Runbook Extractor™
tools.description: Mines a successful agent transcript into a reusable runbook: the steps that worked, retries collapsed into the move that landed, decision branches kept with their triggers, the variables named, and a definition of done — so the next run follows the path instead of rediscovering it.
tools.takes_in: A successful agent run's transcript — the tool calls, the retries, the branch points, and the final result
tools.hands_back: A reusable runbook: ordered steps with retries collapsed, decision branches with their triggers, the variables to fill in, and a definition of done

tools.name: J-Dawgs Uncertainty & Hedge Auditor™
tools.description: Audits a draft agent answer for confidence it has not earned: absolute claims with no evidence, numbers with no source, “verified” without saying what was checked, and strong claims quietly walked back later — then rewrites an honest version that only adds uncertainty wording, never facts.
tools.takes_in: A draft agent answer, pasted as-is — the exact text you are about to send
tools.hands_back: Every unearned-confidence claim flagged — absolute claims with no evidence, numbers with no source, “verified” without saying what was checked, and strong claims quietly walked back later — plus an honest rewrite that only adds uncertainty wording, never facts

tools.name: J-Dawgs Untrusted Content Injection Surface Scanner™
tools.description: LLM Guard needs a Python ML stack installed around a live app; this bench scans one pasted blob of untrusted content in the browser across six injection layers, quotes and explains every flag, and gives a quarantine verdict.
tools.takes_in: One blob of untrusted content — a pasted document, web page text, tool output, or message the agent is about to act on
tools.hands_back: Every injection flag across six layers, quoted and explained, with a quarantine verdict — act on it, strip the flagged parts, or quarantine the whole blob

tools.name: J-Dawgs URL & Link Trust Auditor™
tools.description: Statically audits every URL in a draft before anyone is sent to it: display text checked against the real destination, credentials and token parameters flagged with values masked, punycode and mixed-script hostnames decoded, brand-in-subdomain tricks and shorteners called out — and a SAFE / REVIEW / DO NOT SEND verdict per link. It never fetches or resolves a URL.
tools.takes_in: A draft containing URLs — a message, email, page, or post about to go out — plus your own brand → domain pairs: the brand names to protect and the domains that legitimately belong to each
tools.hands_back: A verdict for every link — SAFE, REVIEW, or DO NOT SEND — with the structural flags behind it: display-text mismatches, credentials and token parameters (values masked everywhere; cleaned URLs returned with them dropped), punycode and mixed-script hostnames decoded and flagged, brands riding in subdomains, shorteners marked destination-hidden, and login links over plain http

tools.name: J-Dawgs Webhook Contract Tester™
tools.description: Paste an expected webhook contract payload and the deliveries that actually arrived: it diffs them field by field — drift, type changes, duplicate event IDs, stale and out-of-order timestamps — and hands back a dedupe skip list.
tools.takes_in: An expected contract payload, plus the actual webhook deliveries to test against it
tools.hands_back: A field-by-field diff — field drift and type changes — plus duplicate event IDs and stale and out-of-order timestamps, and a dedupe skip list of event IDs to drop on sight

tools.name: J-Dawgs Whole-Request Token Estimator™
tools.description: Estimates a whole request payload — messages, tool schemas, and wrapper overhead — not just raw text, with a per-provider fit verdict and an honest uncertainty band on every number.
tools.takes_in: A whole request payload as it will actually be sent — the messages, the tool schemas, and the provider or wrapper it is headed for
tools.hands_back: A token estimate for the whole payload, broken down by part — messages, tool schemas, wrapper overhead — with a per-provider fit verdict and the uncertainty band stated on the number

tools.name: J-Dawgs Workload Re-Pricer™
tools.description: Pricing calculators price imaginary tokens; this re-prices your pasted real usage export across seven model classes with cache and long-context tiers applied, every price stamped with its checked date.
tools.takes_in: A pasted real usage export — the token counts, model names, cache hits, and request volumes from an actual run or billing period
tools.hands_back: The same workload priced across seven model classes with cache and long-context tiers applied, cheapest first, every price stamped with the date it was checked

tools.name: Car Diagnosis by Phone
tools.description: Camera, mic, and OBD data in — a ranked diagnosis out, with the next test to run and what that test rules out.
tools.takes_in: Video of the engine bay, the sound the car makes, trouble codes
tools.hands_back: Likely causes in order, the next test to run, and what each result would prove

tools.name: Fact-Checker for AIs
tools.description: Send it a claim. It checks the claim against a named source and answers with a verdict — and the receipt. Its scope covers verifying exact specs and existence / market claims.
tools.takes_in: A claim: an exact spec (a part number, a fuse size, a price) or an existence / market claim (whether something exists or is really selling for that)
tools.hands_back: Confirmed, corrected, or “can't verify” — plus the source it checked

tools.name: Human Hands for AIs™
tools.description: A board where an AI posts the one physical step it can't do — and a human nearby claims it, does it, and reports back. The board is live and public — visitors can browse the live board now.
tools.takes_in: One physical step, a place, and what “done” looks like
tools.hands_back: A claimed job, then photo proof and a plain report from the human who did it

tools.name: Shoppable Shop Feed
tools.description: A machine-readable version of a real shop, so another AI can read the inventory, check the price, and buy — no human ever opens the page.
tools.takes_in: A shop's listings: item, price, shipping, how to pay
tools.hands_back: A clean feed any AI can search, quote totals from, and order through

free_flagship.name: Almost-JSON Repair Bench — Free Lite Edition
free_flagship.note: Flagship free tool, listed on the store outside the 110-count.
